newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BLAYLOCK LEADS HAWKS TO COMEBACK OT WIN OVER ORLANDO.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BLAYLOCK LEADS HAWKS TO COMEBACK OT WIN OVER ORLANDO.

text.p: Mookie Blaylock made a key steal, hit a pair of free throws with 2.3 seconds left to force overtime, then hit the go-ahead three-pointer in the extra session as the Atlanta Hawks rallied for a 112-107 victory over the Orlando Magic Monday.
Blaylock finished with 18 points, eight assists, seven rebounds and six steals. Steve Smith led the Hawks with 38 points and Christian Laettner added 27.
Penny Hardaway scored 25 of his 35 points after halftime for the Magic, who had their four-game winning streak snapped.

The Hawks, playing without starting centre Dikembe Mutombo who was at home with his expectant wife, trailed by 16 points with 2:30 remaining in the fourth quarter before outscoring the Magic 22-6 to force the overtime and snap their season-high three-game losing streak.

A layup by Laettner got the Hawks within 98-96 with 5.7 seconds remaining in regulation. After a timeout, Blaylock stole Dennis Scott's inbounds pass and was fouled, making both to tie the score. Orlando had a last shot to win in regulation but Derek Strong threw up an airball at the buzzer.
"I never knew it was coming," Blaylock said. "I looked up and I was just right there and stepped in front of it."
"We just turned it up the last few minutes," Laettner said. "Once we got into overtime, the crowd got involved and we played extremely well."

"It's a situation where the game was conceivably out of reach but we did a good job of staying in there and saving time and gave ourselves a chance to win," Tyrone Corbin said. "This is certainly one of the most classic games."
Corbin scored 16 points.
In Charlotte, Karl Malone scored 23 of his 37 points in the second half, when the Utah Jazz exploded for 63 points to claim their fourth straight road win, 114-93 over the Hornets.
John Stockton scored 23 points and Jeff Hornacek added 19 and 12 assists for the Jazz, now 5-1 on their seven-game road trip. Utah trailed by 16 points early in the second period.
Glen Rice scored 29 points and Vlade Divac added 17 and 10 rebounds for Charlotte, which had won seven of its last eight games.

In Cleveland, Tyrone Hill scored a season-high 26 points, including a go-ahead jump hook with 38 seconds left, as the Cavaliers overcame the absence of All-Star point guard Terrell Brandon for an 85-82 victory over the Detroit Pistons.

Chris Mills scored 19 points and Bob Sura added 15 for the Cavaliers, who led by 15 points at halftime but had to erase a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit. Sura started for Brandon, who has a bruised tailbone and is day-to-day.

Otis Thorpe scored 20 points and Grant Hill added 19 for the Pistons, who were held to 26 points in the first half, including nine in the second quarter. It was their second-worst half in franchise history.
In Boston on St Patrick's Day, the Celtics snapped a franchise record-tying seven-game home losing streak with a 126-117 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
Eric Williams scored 25 points, Antoine Walker added 24 and Rick Fox 21 for the Celtics, who used a season high in points to win at the FleetCenter for the first time since January 31.

Glenn Robinson scored 28 points and Vin Baker 25 for the Bucks, who have lost 11 of their last 13 games. Milwaukee gave up a season high in points and lost to Boston for the first time in four games this season.
In Denver, Nick Van Exel scored 30 points including six three-pointers as the Los Angeles Lakers decked the Nuggets 113-94 for their fourth win in five games.
Elden Campbell added 21 points for Los Angeles, which has won all three games against the Nuggets this season.
Antonio McDyess scored 26 points and LaPhonso Ellis 24 for Denver, which has lost five of its last six games.
In San Antonio, Chris Webber scored 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds to lead the Washington Bullets to a 109-85 victory over the Spurs.
Rod Strickland added 16 points and tied a season high with 15 assists for Washington, which has won three of its last four overall and four straight on the road.

Cory Alexander filled in for point guard Avery Johnson, who had throat surgery, and scored a career-high 24 points and tied a career best with 10 assists for San Antonio, which has lost 10 of its last 13.

At Golden State, Jason Kidd scored a season-high 33 points and Kevin Johnson posted his second triple-double of the season with 19 points, 13 assists and 10 rebounds as the Phoenix Suns rallied for a 116-95 victory over the Warriors.
Kidd was 12-of-16 from the floor, including eight three-pointers, and Rex Chapman added 27 points for Phoenix, which has won five of its last six games.
